notes.text: Kailer Yamamoto is on injured reserve and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Clayton Keller has taken his spot beside Anders Lee and Barrett Hayton. That line has had 50% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 34:29 together, down from 75% with Yamamoto.
Nate Schmidt is out (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

story.head: A rematch of last spring’s first round
paras: The Golden Knights have won three straight, while the Mammoth (10-7-1) lost 4-2 to Ottawa on Saturday. Going in, the Mammoth are fifth in the Central (tied for 12th in the NHL) and the Golden Knights second in the Pacific (tied for fifth).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.583) says: their chances are worth about .723, and their goaltending has held them back. The Golden Knights’ record (.684) is about what their chances are worth.

The Mammoth roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (1st). As for the Golden Knights, they draw more penalties than they take (1st) and create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd). They also have one of the league’s best penalty kills (2nd), and the Mammoth’s power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. The Mammoth get in close, but the Knights mostly shoot from distance.

Clayton Keller (5 G / 19 A / 24 P in 18 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Logan Cooley (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 18 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games and eight goals in nine games against Vegas since 2023-24. For the Golden Knights, Jack Eichel (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Mark Stone (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 19 GP) has a team-high ten goals.

Utah has two options in net: Karel Vejmelka (6-6-0 / .867 SV% in 12 GS) and Sebastian Cossa (4-1-1 / .872 SV% in 6 GS). Vejmelka has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Saturday. Vegas also has two options: Adin Hill (7-2-0 / .903 SV% in 9 GS) and Carter Hart (5-3-2 / .900 SV% in 10 GS). Hill has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Sunday. For both teams, it’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

items.text: First meeting since the Golden Knights beat the Mammoth in six games in last spring’s first round, two of them in overtime.

The Mammoth are newly without Nate Schmidt, and have been without Kailer Yamamoto and John Marino for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
The Golden Knights have been without Parker Wotherspoon since Oct 10.
Mitch Marner has three goals on chances worth about 5.3 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
